<reason>Both sides argued with unusual discipline and directly engaged the pressure questions with proper A1/A2 formatting. PRO built a coherent affirmative case around irreversibility, and crucially answered the "why would this time be different" challenge with a concrete mechanism: shifting enforcement from diffuse, hard-to-catch burning to a centralized, dated, satellite-auditable permit/concession chokepoint reinforced by buyer traceability. CON's strongest moves—distinguishing restrictiveness from clarity, insisting leakage and capture are shared weaknesses, and noting that denied expansion income is a real (not merely speculative) loss tied to existing debts and schooling—genuinely damaged PRO's framing and were never fully answered, especially the debt/schooling point raised in B4.6, which PRO's closing did not directly rebut. But CON's own alternative ("enforce existing safeguards plus fund alternatives") remained largely defensive and abstract; CON mostly argued PRO hadn't cleared its burden rather than establishing that enforcement-without-restriction would actually outperform it. PRO's closing crystallized the core asymmetry more memorably and left CON's parity claims looking like they applied "with equal or greater force" to CON's own model. On balance, PRO's affirmative mechanism plus its account of timing (intervening before debt and clearing) gave it a marginally cleaner path to victory, though CON's implementation critiques kept this close rather than lopsided.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>The exchange at [A4.1]/[B4.1]-[B4.5]: PRO's answer that permit chokepoints are centralized and auditable (unlike diffuse burning) versus CON's rejoinder that auditability doesn't force captured officials to act and that the same monitoring tools could reinforce existing safeguards without new restrictions. This exchange, combined with CON's unanswered point at [B4.6] about denied-expansion income harming existing debts/schooling without new debt, was the most decisive clash and the one PRO's closing least fully resolved.</best_rebuttal>
